objectives.text: The BSA aims to combat money laundering and terrorist financing by requiring reports or records useful in criminal, tax or regulatory investigations, risk assessments, proceedings, or intelligence/counterintelligence activities including analysis to protect against terrorism.

citations.quote: The purposes of the BSA include, among others, requiring certain reports or records that are highly useful in criminal, tax or regulatory investigations, risk assessments or proceedings; or intelligence or counterintelligence activities, including analysis, to protect against terrorism.

obligations.action: develop and implement a written anti-money laundering (AML) program that is approved, in writing, by senior management and is reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations

citations.quote: FINRA Rule 3310 (Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Program) requires that each member develop and implement a written anti-money laundering (AML) program that is approved, in writing, by senior management and is reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member’s compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations.

notes: Item is FINRA SRO guidance (evidence role sro_guidance); it restates FINRA Rule 3310 program 'pillars' and cross-references the BSA and implementing regulations, which fall within ratified scope (broker-dealer/FINRA SRO layer, program-establishment obligations). Obligations OBL-3310a through OBL-3310f are the report's enumeration of Rule 3310 minimum standards; the report uses 'requiring firms to:' — modality rendered 'must' from that mandatory framing. The Rule 3310(f) CDD, CIP, SAR/CTR, and correspondent-account due diligence content is treated by the program's scope as coordination/operational layer, but is preserved here as quoted because it is stated as part of the program pillars. External fraud schemes, GenAI fraud, and effective practices are largely non-obligatory (described as practices 'firms may consider' / 'to consider'); only clearly modal statements were extracted as obligations. Rule 2165 (may) and CAB 331 (conditional) captured as modal duties. The report is guidance restating obligations, not itself the primary source of statutory/regulatory duty; citations preserve the report's own phrasing per fidelity rule. The independent-testing threshold contains an internal alternative ('each calendar year (or every two calendar years in some specialized cases)') preserved as written.
